fine_trace.note: The only pre-copy guard verifies that 4 bytes remain, but the null-terminated branch immediately below copies 5 bytes (memcpy(&c, it, 5)). For the trailing truncated token 'tur' exactly 4 bytes remain (including the harness-appended null terminator), so the guard passes although 5 bytes are about to be read; the needed safety condition size_t(end - it) >= 5 is never enforced.

Attacker-controlled bytes at the boolean token position are copied into c; the input '[true,true,tur' is parsed as an array whose last element 'tur' is a truncated boolean token sitting at the very end of the buffer, so this is where the input bytes become the program value consumed by the boolean parser.

The unconditional 5-byte copy reads one byte past end (only 4 bytes remain in the null-terminated buffer) into the vector's unused capacity region, which ASan poisons for container-overflow detection - the out-of-bounds read that crashes the target.
